item: a restore finds a law document under any spelling of its jurisdiction, so an old backup over a new paste is one row
summary: The restore matched law_documents by the exact text of (jurisdiction, url), so a backup the old paste route wrote (gb, GBR, euu, ant, uae, drc) restored over a document pasted after PR #1679 added a second row (6 pairs into an alpha-2 store, 8 into an alpha-3 store went from one row to two). Both sides are now compared through law_jurisdiction_key (the catalogue's form for a code of two or three ASCII letters, the string as stored for anything else), keyed once in Python into indexed temp tables for the duplicate count, the INSERT and the id map; nothing is rewritten and a word (france, georgia, congo) is never guessed into a code. A staged document that shares its identity with another staged one (a backup holding one document under two spellings) is matched by its exact spelling as before, which keeps the id map one-to-one (the first version mapped both onto one row and the whole restore failed on UNIQUE(document_id, content_hash); found by the independent read). The merge's placing of an alternate and the app's later lookup choose the document by the same ordering (the spelling the identity names, else the oldest); the paste route shares the code shape and the key with the restore. Stated limits: stored rows are not rewritten; a word on one install and a code on another stay two rows; an alternate's recorded spelling is converted to the store's form before it is compared, as before. 282 tests (127 red on the unchanged merge), 42 mutants all killed, two independent reads, 13,408 differential cases (26,816 restores) against the unchanged merge with no new failure.
